title: systemd stalls activating LVM swap after a udev-less custom initramfs
body: I am using systemd 255 on x86_64 and have reproduced this across Fedora, Debian, Ubuntu, and Gentoo with various kernels. I boot without udev and activate LVM volumes with the LVM tools. After boot, systemd hangs while looking for the udev device path for an LVM swap volume even though the volume is mapped and listed in fstab. The swap is not activated, and I expect it to be activated so the system can finish booting normally.

symptoms_visible: After the LVM volumes are mapped, systemd waits for a udev device path and the LVM swap from fstab is not activated.
N0.label: N0 LVM swap activation stall reported

symptoms_visible: My shell-based initramfs mounts the encrypted LVM root and completes switch_root, but the main system then stalls on the LVM swap.
The swap is not activated by the initramfs; running swapon -a after boot activates it.
N1.label: N1 initramfs and swap ownership clarified

symptoms_visible: A clean reboot stalls while waiting for the swap device; the mapper entry is present, but the swap unit does not become active until I run swapon.
N2.label: N2 clean reboot and unit state captured

symptoms_visible: The same boot still waits for the LVM swap device, while manual swapon remains able to activate it.
N3.label: N3 debug journal collected

symptoms_visible: Even with vgscan --mknodes creating valid-looking entries under /dev/mapper, automatic swap activation still waits for the device.
N3_x.label: N3_x mapper-node workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: Automatic activation of the LVM swap has not been confirmed fixed on my system; noauto with manual swapon is available as a workaround.
N_terminal.label: terminal external diagnosis without reporter verification

question_patterns: Is udev disabled only in the initrd, and what runs as init there?
Does your initramfs run systemd or udevd?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My ugrd initramfs does not run systemd or udevd. It runs a simple shell script whose job is to prepare the root filesystem.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: systemd-udevd is disabled in the real root as well, so no udev daemon runs after switch_root.

question_patterns: Is the root filesystem also on LVM, and does the stall happen before or after switch_root?
Please describe exactly what the initramfs activates before handing over to the real root.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The initramfs autodetects and activates the LUKS/LVM root, mounts it, and performs switch_root. That part works. The stall happens afterward, when the main systemd instance is running.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The initramfs itself stalls before mounting the LVM root or reaching switch_root.
The same shell initramfs and post-switch_root stall occur with an equivalent Fedora encrypted-LVM layout.

question_patterns: Please provide the fstab and disk layout for the affected system.
What LVM and encrypted-volume layout are you using?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This is the default disk layout made by the Debian installer for its encrypted setup, which I am using as a reference. The screenshot shows the layout.

question_patterns: After switch_root, are systemd and systemd-udevd actually running?
Can you check whether udevd starts in the real root?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, systemd runs after switch_root and I think udevd is running there; this screenshot is what I see on the Debian system.

question_patterns: Does your initrd call swapon or otherwise enable the swap before switch_root?
Is the swap already active when the real systemd instance starts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. The initramfs ignores swap and exists only to mount the root and switch_root. I want the main init system to activate the fstab swap.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The swap is already active before switch_root, and systemd only fails to recognize that active swap.

question_patterns: Can the swap be activated manually after the boot stall?
What happens if you run swapon -a?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Running swapon -a activates the swap successfully after boot. The swap-service screenshot was taken after I had done that.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: swapon -a fails with an invalid swap signature or an I/O error.

edges.comment: Reporter setup from c6, c10-c13: this is the reporter's custom ugrd initramfs and Debian encrypted-LVM test system. It activates the root without udev, then hands off to systemd and udevd in the real root; swap is deliberately left for the main init system.

question_patterns: Please reboot and show systemctl cat, status, and show for the swap unit before running swapon.
Can you capture the swap unit state from a clean boot before manually enabling it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I rebooted without running swapon first. The boot stalls waiting for the swap device, and the swap unit is not active in the post-reboot output.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After a clean reboot the swap unit is already active and the boot does not wait for a device.
The same unit waits under a different generated unit name corresponding to the same LVM swap path.

question_patterns: Are the expected device-mapper entries present under /dev/mapper after the reboot?
Please show the mapped root, swap, and crypt device nodes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The mapped entries exist for debian--vg-root, debian--vg-swap_1, and vda3_crypt.

question_patterns: Does a fresh reboot reliably reproduce the wait before any manual swapon command?
Please confirm the boot behavior immediately after reboot.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. It stalls at the device wait during boot before I manually activate the swap.

question_patterns: After the failed automatic activation, what does the unit show once you run swapon manually?
Can you show whether manual swapon changes the observed swap state?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After the stalled boot, I can activate the swap with swapon and it then shows as active.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c14-c17 on the same Debian VM: participant1 requested a reboot and pre-swapon unit output. The c17 screenshots cover the pre-reboot state, boot wait, initrd console, post-reboot state, and successful manual activation.

question_patterns: Please reboot with systemd.log_level=debug and upload the root system journal from journalctl --no-hostname -b.
Can you collect the full system journal with debug logging, using sudo so it includes PID 1 and udev messages?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I added systemd.log_level=debug through GRUB, rebooted, and uploaded the journal. My first upload only contained the user journal, so I reran journalctl with sudo and uploaded XOdP.txt.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I uploaded the same user-only journal again, with no PID 1 or systemd-udevd entries.

question_patterns: What raw udev and PID 1 messages does the debug journal contain for the swap's dm device?
Please paste the relevant dm device processing lines from the debug journal.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For dm-2, the journal says the add event was queued and processed, /dev/block/254:2 was linked to /dev/dm-2, and the udev database file was created. It then says: 'systemd[1]: dm-2: Device busy: SYSTEMD_READY property from device is false'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The journal shows SYSTEMD_READY=1, includes the expected mapper path in the udev event, and PID 1 immediately marks the device ready.
The same messages appear for a different dm minor number assigned to the swap on the next boot.

edges.comment: Reporter measurement from c18-c24, with raw lines later quoted in c28. The reporter supplied the debug journal; identifying the missing mapper-path metadata and assigning responsibility to the initrd/LVM rules are engineer conclusions reserved for the final solution.

solution.intent: Create the missing /dev/mapper nodes by running vgscan --mknodes in the custom initramfs before switch_root.
solution.concrete_example: Run vgscan --mknodes after activating the volume group so /dev/mapper/debian--vg-swap_1 exists before handing off to systemd.

edges.comment: Reporter c29-c31 on the same ugrd setup: vgscan --mknodes was already added to the initramfs and left in place. It produces valid-looking mapper entries, but automatic swap activation still waits because node existence alone does not supply the udev metadata/event association expected by PID 1.

solution.intent: Treat this as an initramfs/LVM udev-integration problem rather than a systemd swap-unit bug: ensure device-mapper volumes are processed with usable udev metadata before handoff, or synthesize and replay equivalent udev state; use noauto plus manual swapon only as a workaround, and verify automatic activation on a reboot before declaring it fixed.
solution.concrete_example: Have the custom initramfs activate LVM through udev-aware handling, or record and recreate the necessary udev database/event information for the mapper devices before switch_root. Merely creating /dev/mapper nodes is insufficient. Until that integration is corrected, mark the swap noauto and run swapon manually, then retest a normal reboot after implementing the metadata/event fix.
solution.inference_hint: The engineer inferred from the uploaded journal that although udev processed dm-2, PID 1 received SYSTEMD_READY=false without usable notification tying the expected /dev/mapper path to a ready device. The final accepted diagnosis places the problem in the custom initramfs/LVM-device-rule handoff, not in systemd's generated swap unit. The reporter supplied raw journal lines and later confirmed that vgscan --mknodes only creates nodes; they did not independently derive the full readiness-state mechanism.

edges.comment: Final diagnosis from participant1 c27-c34 for the reporter's original LVM-swap setup. The issue was closed as not a systemd/udevd bug and referred to the initrd/LVM udev-rule integration; noauto plus manual swapon was offered as a workaround. Reporter c35 and c38 later discussed recording or fabricating udev state, but the thread contains no confirmation that the original reporter retested automatic LVM swap activation successfully, so the terminal state remains unverified.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted cause: LVM device-mapper volumes were activated in the custom initramfs before udev processing, and the later udev event did not provide PID 1 with the mapper-path readiness information it needed; the journal consequently reports SYSTEMD_READY=false.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected clean-reboot unit state and debug journal, including that mapper nodes exist and manual swapon works; it must not infer a bad swap signature or missing block device from the symptom alone.
Must not present vgscan --mknodes or merely creating /dev/mapper entries as the fix, because those nodes were already created and automatic activation still waited.

The durable direction must address the custom initramfs/LVM udev handoff by using udev-aware activation or supplying equivalent udev database and event information; noauto with manual swapon may be offered only as a workaround.

Must ask the reporter to verify automatic swap activation on a reboot after changing the initramfs or LVM integration, and must not claim the original system was resolved because no such reporter verification appears in the thread.

persona_hint.experience_level: Advanced Linux user and initramfs-tool author who understands LUKS, LVM, switch_root, fstab, device nodes, and shell-based early boot, but is less familiar with systemd unit generation and udev's readiness database semantics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, direct, and design-oriented; supplies screenshots and logs when asked, challenges architectural requirements that seem unnecessary, and clearly distinguishes what the initramfs does from what the main init system should do.
